skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guides root-cause debugging through evidence gathering, pattern comparison, hypothesis testing, and verified implementation.
skill.summary: Investigate software failures systematically before implementing focused, tested fixes.
skill.author: davila7

remediation.suggestion: Use presence-only checks, redact values, and warn users before printing CI environment or keychain metadata.

content.value_statement: Guessing at fixes wastes time and often creates new failures. This skill guides evidence-based root-cause analysis before focused implementation and verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides a four-phase workflow from investigation through verified implementation.
Helps reproduce failures and inspect errors, recent changes, dependencies, and component boundaries.
Traces invalid data backward through call chains to identify original triggers.
Forms one testable hypothesis and recommends the smallest experiment that can confirm it.
Shows condition-based waiting techniques for reducing flaky asynchronous tests.
Includes a shell script for identifying tests that create unwanted files or state.
limitations: It does not automatically reproduce failures or inspect systems without available tools and user authorization.
Its examples focus mainly on TypeScript, shell commands, and test infrastructure.
Domain-specific failures still require knowledge of the application, platform, and dependencies.
The full workflow may be slower than immediate mitigation during an active incident.

use_cases.title: Resolve Recurring Application Bugs
use_cases.description: Trace a repeated failure from its visible symptom to the originating input, state change, or dependency.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Flaky Test Suites
use_cases.description: Replace arbitrary delays with condition checks and isolate tests that create shared files or state.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Multi-Service Incidents
use_cases.description: Add focused diagnostics at component boundaries and identify where data or configuration stops propagating correctly.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Basic Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging for this failure: [error]. Identify reproduction steps, evidence to gather, and one root-cause hypothesis before proposing a fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner investigation of a reproducible error

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Flaky Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this flaky test: [details]. Find every arbitrary wait, define observable completion conditions, and propose a minimal reliability experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Invalid Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this invalid value backward through the call chain: [trace]. Identify its source and recommend validation at appropriate layers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced root-cause tracing across application layers

prompt_templates.title: Reassess Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failed fix attempts: [attempts]. Determine whether the evidence supports a new hypothesis or indicates an architectural problem requiring discussion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging after repeated unsuccessful changes

output_examples.input: A payment test sometimes remains pending after a fixed delay.
output: Observed symptom: status remains pending after an arbitrary wait.
Evidence needed: completion event timing, state transition logs, and reproduction frequency.
Hypothesis: the test checks state before the asynchronous completion event.
Experiment: wait for the completion event instead of increasing the delay.

output_examples.input: A project command creates repository metadata in the source directory.
output: Immediate cause: the command receives an empty working directory.
Trace target: identify where the empty value entered the call chain.
Focused fix: validate the source value before workspace creation.
Defense: reject unsafe directories at entry, business, and environment boundaries.

output_examples.input: Three attempted fixes moved the failure to different modules.
output_examples.output: The repeated cross-module failures suggest shared coupling or an unsound architecture. Stop adding patches and review the design with the responsible team.

best_practices: Capture the exact error, reproduction steps, and recent changes before editing code.
Test one specific hypothesis with the smallest possible change.
Verify the original failure and the wider test suite after implementing the root-cause fix.
anti_patterns: Do not stack several speculative fixes into one test run.
Do not replace unexplained timing failures with longer arbitrary delays.
Do not stop at the visible symptom when the triggering input can be traced.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for bugs, test failures, build problems, performance issues, integration errors, and other unexpected technical behavior.

faq.question: Does the skill fix code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It structures investigation and implementation, while available tools and user permissions determine which actions can run.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends condition-based waiting, observable completion signals, timeouts, and test isolation.

faq.question: What happens when a hypothesis is wrong?
faq.answer: Record the result, return to the evidence, and form a new single hypothesis instead of adding another speculative change.

faq.question: What should happen after three failed fixes?
faq.answer: Stop implementing patches and discuss whether shared state, coupling, or architecture is causing the repeated failures.

faq.question: Does it replace incident mitigation procedures?
faq.answer: No. Teams should follow approved mitigation and rollback procedures while preserving evidence for later root-cause analysis.
